title: Pain Hours After Welding

patient.name: Mr Muthu Kumar
patient.presenting_complaint: Both eyes very painful, gritty and watering since the middle of the night, after welding earlier in the day without a proper visor

history.hpc: Mr Muthu was welding in the afternoon without a proper visor. He says: 'In the afternoon I do welding, then midnight my eyes super pain, like sand inside, cannot open, keep tearing.' Both eyes are red and very light-sensitive. The pain after welding is typically delayed by several hours — this fits a flash burn (welder's flash / photokeratitis).
history.social_hx: Welder; not using adequate eye protection at the time.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Both eyes: conjunctival redness, tearing, marked photophobia; corneal surface irritation consistent with flash burn

investigations.front_line_triage: Recognise the delayed-onset painful red eyes after welding as a flash burn (welder's flash) — a Category 3 presentation (painful red eye / flash burn; assess within 60 minutes). Triage appropriately (urgent but not Category 1), keep the patient comfortable in reduced lighting, and refer to the doctor.
investigations.va_distance: Both eyes mildly reduced due to tearing/photophobia.

diagnosis: Bilateral flash burn (photokeratitis) from welding without eye protection — painful red eyes with the classic delayed onset. Triaged as Category 3 (painful red eye / flash burn). The PSA competency is recognising the mechanism and pattern, triaging correctly, comforting the patient, and referring to the doctor.

immediate: Recognise the welding mechanism with delayed-onset pain as a flash burn
Triage as Category 3 (painful red eye / flash burn — within 60 minutes)
Keep the patient comfortable in dimmed lighting to ease photophobia
Do not instil drops without the doctor's order; advise not to rub the eyes
Refer to the doctor for assessment and pain relief
Document the mechanism, time of welding vs onset, symptoms, and triage category
follow_up: Doctor to examine, provide pain relief, and manage the corneal surface injury
Advise on recovery and the importance of proper eye protection
Record the triage outcome on the SNEC triage form
patient_education: Explain that the pain came hours later because that is typical of a welding flash burn
Reassure him the surface usually heals, and the doctor will help with the pain
Advise dim lighting and not rubbing the eyes while waiting
Strongly advise a proper welding visor/eye protection to prevent recurrence
